brief_rule: Recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy; each brief names the trait kept and the trait changed.
inspiration: Behaviour as a small library of data nodes (sequence, selector, guard, timeout, loop, counter, invert), each with a name, category and one-line description. For row 2, express the brain as a few data nodes (aggro gate, give-up timer, patrol loop) instead of hard-coded branches. File: engine/src/main/resources/org/terasology/engine/assets/prefabs/behaviorActions/guard.prefab.

Damage type as data: the physical hit type carries an impulse value, so knock-back belongs to the hit type. For row 10, keep knock-back as a field of the hit and tune our own numbers with hitstop. File: engine/src/main/resources/org/terasology/engine/assets/prefabs/damageTypes/physicalDamage.prefab.

Death screen as one centred column: a title, a details line, a spacer, then a stacked button column with respawn first. For row 17, keep the single prominent respawn at the top and put the cause of the loss in the details line; change the wording and add a short grace before the button enables. File: engine/src/main/resources/org/terasology/engine/assets/ui/ingame/deathScreen.ui.

Sound variation pools: six slime clips and five grass-footstep clips chosen at random so repeats are rare. For row 12, a hit-sound pool of five per impact class, recreated from scratch. Files: engine/src/main/resources/org/terasology/engine/assets/sounds/Slime1.ogg to Slime6.ogg (not opened).

Block shapes as a small preset library (stair, half, eighth, slope, trimmed raised cube) stored as data. For zone geometry and arena steps, a few stepped and sloped presets picked by name. Files: engine/src/main/resources/org/terasology/engine/assets/shapes/stair.shape and shapes/slopes/ (not opened).

Radial item picker folder (textures/ui/radial) and a tree-view icon set sit next to the editor icons. For the phone inspect flow and quick item selection, a radial picker with its own icon style. File: engine/src/main/resources/org/terasology/engine/assets/textures/ui/radial/ (not opened).

briefs.label: Radial quick-pick ring
briefs.why: A ring of small icons around a centre point gives a fast pick under thumb pressure and reads at 375 wide if the ring is big enough. It suits quick item or spell choice in a fight.
briefs.keep: Round layout around a centre; icon-first with no text; one icon per slot.
briefs.change: Use our own icon style and palette; use a fan of 4-6 slots instead of a full ring; open on hold, not on click.
briefs.ref: engine/src/main/resources/org/terasology/engine/assets/textures/ui/radial/ (folder read by name only; not opened)

briefs.label: Death column with a grace button
briefs.why: A calm column after a loss (title, one line of cause, then stacked actions) makes a loss readable instead of abrupt. The respawn action sits first and is the obvious next step.
briefs.keep: Title, one details line, spacer, respawn first; centred stacked column.
briefs.change: Show the killer and the zone in the details line; add a 3-second arm delay on respawn; replace the settings button with a loot-recovery summary.

briefs.label: Pool-of-five hit sound
briefs.why: Several variants of one impact stop the ear noticing repetition in a long duel. The file names show the pool pattern (six slime, five footstep); I did not open the audio, so the variation itself is unverified.
briefs.keep: Pool of 5-6 per action class; random pick with no immediate repeat.
briefs.change: Make our own sounds; pick by impact class (block, hit, crit) not by creature name; add a pitch band of 3 semitones.

briefs.label: Knock-back carried by the hit type
briefs.why: Putting the impulse on the damage type lets one hit definition push differently in different fights, which suits a data-driven catalogue of hits.
briefs.keep: Impulse is a field of the hit type; a hit type can be reused by many attackers.
briefs.change: Add hitstop before the impulse; cap the impulse per target size; name the hit type for our moves, not the Terasology ones.

briefs.label: Stepped and sloped arena presets
briefs.why: A few named geometry presets (step, half, slope) let an arena designer add cover and height quickly, and a silhouette of stairs and slopes reads well at small size.
briefs.keep: Named shape presets stored as data; a slope and a step set.
briefs.change: Use our own preset names and proportions; a 45 degree ramp and a low wall only; no voxel grid.
